completedTasks.title: A call to a tool this server does not have is answered with the tool to call
completedTasks.summary: 2.0.0 renamed every MCP tool and shipped no aliases, so a client still speaking the old names got the SDK's own JSON-RPC -32602 ('Unknown tool: memory_search') and nothing it could act on. Such a call is now a normal tool error (CallToolResult.IsError = true) with the wire prefix 'unknown-tool': a pre-2.0.0 name is answered with the name to call instead ('unknown-tool: \'memory_search\' was renamed to \'query\' in 2.0.0 - call \'query\' instead.'), any other name with the general message. The surface decides what exists (McpToolInventory, generated from the [McpServerTool] declarations), the rename map is the 2.0.0 changelog's table and a test compares the two, the refusal is logged at Information like every other expected failure, and the old names stay dead - this is an answer, not an alias. ADR-0140, VERSION 2.0.1.

The design basis is that record, not rtk's implementation - rtk-proxy is BUSL-1.1 and no rtk code is vendored. v1 (the router, the forwarder, the credential rule, the pass-through) is queued as the continuation step in the new repo's state.json. Three defects were found by running the gates rather than reading them: the pre-push gate printed FAIL but exited 0 (an `if` without an `else` returns 0), CI failed with NU1301 because the workflow did not create the gitignored .nupkg-local feed nuget.config references, and a renamed CI job would have blocked every PR with no gate to notice.

completedTasks.title: The tool scope is an enum (All/Shared/Project) and a Roslyn analyzer owns the missing-scope error
completedTasks.summary: The owner's correction (f:) on PR #907: RequiresOrdinaryProject became a scope definition by enum - All, Shared, Project - and the 'a tool with no scope' error moved out of the source generator into a real Roslyn DiagnosticAnalyzer. The rule is symmetric: a tool's scope must cover the target's scope, the reserved target's scope being Shared and an ordinary project's Project. All = any target (the 16 tools that may use the reserved target), Project = ordinary projects only (the 14 ordinary-only tools, memory_delete among them), Shared = the reserved target only (no tool uses it yet, and the rule that honours it is tested rather than assumed). An undeclared tool name is Project, so the default-deny that shipped is unchanged and no caller's behaviour moved. The one-sided rule could not express a Shared-scoped tool at all - it read 'may not be the reserved target' and nothing more - and the new test for that case is the red the symmetric rule answers. ToolScopeAnalyzer (AIRGEN002) now reports the error at the tool's own declaration; the generator emits only the classification; both share one definition of what a tool is (ToolScopeFacts), which the build enforces too, since one diagnostic id cannot be declared twice (RS1019). Evidence: the shape change kept the suite green with the 14/16 split unchanged; the symmetric rule was red first and is green now; the generator's ownership was reconstructed as a red and recorded as such; the analyzer's test was mutation-checked (neutered: 3/1 failed, restored: 3/0); removing the declaration from code_get gives exactly one AIRGEN002 at CodeTools.cs(21,51). The correction also caught that the first diagnostic message tripped RS1032 - the analyzer rules read the '. ' as two sentences - which breaks a solution build, and a solution build is what CI runs, so the enum step on its own was not mergeable. Gates: solution build 0 errors 0 warnings; generator project 7/0; MCP unit surface 326/0; shared-project integration 19/0; docs unit surface 26/0; whole Unit category 4303/0 with 1 skipped.

completedTasks.title: The MCP tool scope is declared on the tool and compiled; the reserved shared target refuses memory_delete
completedTasks.summary: The review of PR #906 (docs/work/2026-10-21-pr906-scope-check-review.md) found that ToolNameScope's hand-written list of 7 names plus 2 prefix families default-allowed every name not on it, with nothing comparing it to the generated tool inventory, and that memory_delete - the one destructive tool allowed on the reserved shared target - was unspecified in ADR-0137 and the operator reference. The scope is now declared on each of the 30 tool methods with [McpToolScope(RequiresOrdinaryProject: ...)] and compiled by the existing Roslyn generator from the same candidate pass that gathers the tool surface: a tool that declares no scope is a build error (AIRGEN002), the hand-written list and both prefix families are gone, the generated file is data only and a thin ToolNameScope implements IToolNameScope over it, and a name that is not a declared tool is refused (the default flipped from allow to deny; it has one caller, and it only ever sees a declared tool's own name). memory_delete is refused on the reserved target: its content is owned by the watch and the file, and a delete there removed only the chunk whose hash was named (measured: rows_before=4 rows_after=3 deleted=1), advanced no watch fingerprint, and left the digest hash-skipping on a file it still claimed was current. ADR-0139 records the decision, ADR-0137 is amended (its CanSearchCode sentence named a method removed in 3849135e), the ADR index is updated - it is a derived mirror with a gate, so the 0139 row, the 0137 Amended cell and a 0138 skip row are part of the change - and the operator reference names the refusal. Evidence: 3 failing tests written first (the scope pin, the generator diagnostic, the reserved target's delete through the real tool), 2 mutations seen red and then green, the whole Unit surface 4302/0, the shared-project integration 19/0, AdrIndexTests 7/0. The plan review and the implementation review both ran; the plan review's 6 MUST findings were folded in, and one of the implementation review's two claims was checked against the source and found not to hold. VERSION 1.63.0. PR #907.

completedTasks.title: The observability counters command names every exported counter, and the CLI documents the verb
completedTasks.summary: From the research record (docs/work/2026-10-19-observability-counters-cli-coverage.md): 'serve observability counters' printed 'dotnet-counters monitor -p <pid>', and an unspecified --counters makes dotnet-counters default to System.Runtime, so the pasted command showed GC/CPU/working set and none of the server's own instruments while the server was serving tool calls. The rendered command now carries --counters with string.Join(',', OtlpNames.Meters) (AiRaccoon.MemoryTools, AiRaccoon.PromotionQueue, AiRaccoon.Background, System.Runtime, System.Net.Http), derived from the list the DI registry guard keeps honest; the string golden is replaced by a contract test over that list, and the integration test asserts the runner's stdout against the renderer. The observability help and its kind argument now say what each kind prints, pinned by a test, and the CLI reference, the agent-memory-server reference, ADR-0008 and the how-to guide agree with the code. Proven against a live server: the printed line pasted into dotnet-counters shows [AiRaccoon.MemoryTools], [AiRaccoon.Background] and [System.Runtime] with ai_raccoon.tool.invocations and mcp.server.operation.duration, where the old line showed [System.Runtime] only. PR #893 merged as f1411686, followed by five review-driven follow-ups: #895 (ADR-0008's amendment record, the how-to's in-session caveat, the test's comment), #896 (the OtlpNames.Meters role comment), #897 (the doc-sync guard), #898 (the strengthened contract split and help check), #899 (the no-bank invariant test, the kind-to-yield pairing, the wording fix, and the root help naming the monitoring verb) — the last merged as 6c3b9d2d. Two delegated review lanes ran and both returned SHIP WITH THE SHOULD FIXES: the plan review (a contract test in both directions, the full integration assertion, 1.60.2 as the patch level, the four documentation surfaces moving with the code) and the implementation review (a stronger flag split in the contract test, a stronger help assertion). completedTasks.title: Context key total over a NULL project id; stored vec-trigger bodies replaced (ADR-0124, 1.53.13)
completedTasks.summary: vec0's metadata ctx rejects NULL, while MemorySql.ContextKeyExpression returned SQL NULL for project_id IS NULL (its C# twin never did): the vec_entries_au/vec_structure_au triggers threw at MarkEmbedded (ADR-0119 charged 3 attempts then abandoned the row), the v9 rebuild's rethrow blocked opening a v2-v8 bank holding such a row, and pre-v9 partition keys accepted the NULL. Fix: COALESCE(project_id,'') in every concatenating branch (key total: project:/custom:0::L/workspace:0::W, equal to ContextKeyFor(_, '')) plus an every-open probe-first replacement of the two stored trigger bodies from shared constants (EnsureVecCtxTriggerBodiesAsync, ADR-0023 amendment shape) — CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS cannot replace an existing bank's body, and the live bank's bodies carried the old expression. No migration (verified: vec0 0.1.9 rejects NULL metadata; pre-v9 rows are rebuilt by v9; live bank 0 NULL/'' ctx). 8 RED-first tests; the plan review caught the stored-body blocker; both implementation reviews folded (consumer table, IS rationale, sibling statement-count gate). 1.53.13.

MCP protocol CallToolResult.IsError is null on success (absent), true only on failure — assert ShouldNotBe(true), not ShouldBe(false)
Bare `ai-raccoon` is a proxy: it opens no bank, resolves no key and loads no ONNX model. `--transport stdio` is the in-process server and the escape hatch when a backend cannot start

`serve` mints <data-root>/mcp-token (0600) BEFORE it binds, so a port that answers guarantees the file exists; the probe accepts 401 as proof of a live server so it still recognises one across data roots

/mcp and /shutdown accept the loopback token in either envelope: X-AiRaccoon-Token or Authorization: Bearer *** one credential compared with FixedTimeEquals on both paths and neither shadowing the other. /mcp alone renders a second 401 body for a credential that was presented but did not match; /shutdown keeps one body for every failure because ADR-0022 pins the refusal not to reveal whether a token exists. `serve --mcp-entry` prints a headers map carrying ${AIRACCOON_MCP_TOKEN}, never a live token - Hermes resolves it from ~/.hermes/.env, Claude Code from the environment, and an unset variable in Claude Code warns in `claude mcp list` but still sends the literal placeholder.

The manifest is the budget source of truth: chunkTokens (1022) sets memory chunk size AND the query-trim budget; code chunks stay 510 (min(510, ctx-2)). Everything that says 'longer than one chunk' or pins the manifest must follow it — scripts/src/bundle.py's BUNDLED_MANIFEST pin (guarded by scripts/tests/test_bundle.py::test_committed_files_match_their_pins) and every chunk-count fixture derive from the manifest, never literals.

ChunkBudgetReconciler (EntryEmbedder drain, after vec reconcile, before the embed loop): re-chunks AND re-embeds at the resolved budget; embedding.chunkBudget stamp present iff the last run converged; unproven note groups get 3 passes per resolved budget then stop gating (residual population named in ADR-0125); terminal skips never gate; event 448 reports counts.

Long-blocking tool calls in delegated lanes kill the session ('aborted (lost)' — observed 3x at dotnet-test full-suite launches; the dotnet-engineer persona's sonnet/bedrock pin also has no API key and falls back to openrouter). Lane briefs must mandate detached runs + tail polling and commit-as-you-go.
